newsitem.title: GERMANY: F.O. LICHT - Daily sugar report.
newsitem.headline: F.O. LICHT - Daily sugar report.

text.p: The following is a direct contribution from statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.

White sugar futures in London closed lower but above lows, boosted by a stronger performance on the New York raw sugar market late in the day. March finished $0.20 lower at $309.10 while May gave up $0.50 to close at $308.20. In New York raw sugar futures closed weaker but above lows hit early when funds failed to follow through and mixed selling pressured prices. Both March and May gave up 6 points and ended at 10.94 cents/lb. There was no fresh fundamental news to influence prices.

INDIA - Indian sugar production in November 1996 reached 764,130 tonnes, raw value, significantly down on last year's figure of 1.277 million tonnes. This brought cumulative production in the first two months of 1996/97 to 1.478 million tonnes, which compares to 1.480 million tonnes produced in the same two months the previous year. Deliveries for domestic consumption in November 1996 reached 1.261 million tonnes, raw value, which compares to 1.260 million tonnes the same two months in 1995. Despatches for export in November 1996 totalled 67,000 tonnes, raw value, compared with 61,000 tonnes the same month in 1995. Sugar stocks on November 30 stood at 6.6 million tonnes, up from 4.92 million tonnes the same date in 1995.

SPAIN - Sugar imports in September 1996 amounted to 32,585 tonnes, raw value, down from last year's 44,121 tonnes. This brought cumulative imports in the first quarter of 1996/97 (July/September) to 115,832 tonnes against 89,007 tonnes in the like period the previous year. Total imports in 1995/96 amounted to 353,193 tonnes compared to 257,273 in 1994/95. Major countries of origin in July/September 1996 were France with 78,207 tonnes whites against 59,231 and Germany with 10,205 tonnes, down from 13,998. Sugar exports in September 1996 reached 38,948 tonnes, up from 14,814 in September 1995. This brought cumulative exports in July/September 1996 to 61,570 tonnes vs 87,784 tonnes in July/September 1995. Total exports in 1995/96 amounted to 208,130 tonnes, up from 195,960 in 1994/95. Major countries of destination in July/September 1996 were Tunisia with 15,301 tonnes whites, down from 22,034 tonnes and Senegal with 12,182 tonnes against negligible amounts in 1995.

THAILAND - According to ISO figures, Thai sugar exports in September 1996 reached 73,912 tonnes, raw value, down from 166,196 tonnes in September 1995. Total exports in 1995/96 (November/October) amounted to 4.656 million tonnes compared to 3.847 million tonnes in 1994/95 and 2.802 million in 1993/94. Major countries of destination in November/September 1995/96 were Japan with 747,142 tonnes raws against 491,982, Korea with 635,494 tonnes up from 379,552 tonnes and China with 524,164 tonnes, down from 1.228 million tonnes. The largest outlets for Thai white sugar in 1995/96 were Indonesia with 590,141 tonnes, up from 306,595, and Iran with 307,410 tonnes against 104,834.
